full_judgment:
Amirul Kabir Chowdhury J: Accused petitioner Md. Shahidul @ Sahidul Hossain Hannan seeks leave to appeal against the judgment and order dated 29.01.2006 passed by the High Court Division in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 13882 of 2005 making the rule absolute thereby transferring the case from the court of Druto Bichar Tribunal No.1, Dhaka to Druto Bichar Tribunal No.2 at Dhaka. 

 2. On 01.03.2004 one Anowaruzzaman lodged a First Information Report with Dhanmondi Police Station to the effect that his elder brother Khairul Anwar Piaru president of Dhanmondi Club was returning from the Club on 29.02.2004 at about 10 P.M. accompanied by Ansar Commander Shamsul Alam and while reached the main gate of the club at Road No. 8A of Dhanmondi Residential Area some miscreants in order to kill him fired shots which hit his brother on his head and other parts of the body and Ansar Commander Shamsul Alam was also injured and that the miscreants fled away thereafter and the victim Khairul Anwar Piaru was taken to Dhaka Medical College Hospital where he was declared as dead. On the basis of the aforesaid First Information Report Dhanmondi P.S. Case No.1 dated 01.03.2004 was started and the police after investigation submitted charge sheet against the accused petitioner and others under Sections 326/302/109/34 of the Penal Code on 16.03.2005. The Government by notification in the official gazette transferred the cases for trial before the Druto Bichar Tribunal No.1, Dhaka. 

 3. During pendency of the trial the accused petitioner filed an application under Section 526 of the Code of Criminal Procedure read with Section 4(4) of the Druto Bichar Tribunal Ain, 2002 praying to transfer the case from Druto Bichar Tribunal No.1, Dhaka to any other competent court at Dhaka. 

 4. The High Court Division by the impugned judgment and order made the rule absolute and transferred the case as already mentioned above. 

 6. In support of the petition Mr. Abdul Baset Majumder, learned Counsel submits, inter alia, that the High Court division while passing the impugned judgment and order has gone contrary to the provision of Section 4(4) of Druto Bichar Tribunal Ain, 2002 and that jurisdiction of the tribunal to try a case being determined by the Government under Section 5 of the Ain, the instant order of transfer has been made contrary to the said provision of law and as such cannot be maintained. 

 7. Mr. A.J. Mohammad Ali, learned Attorney General opposes the petition submitting, inter-alia, that the instant petition has been filed with oblique motive to delay and drag the disposal of the case as previously also a number of applications have been unsuccessfully filed at the instance of accused persons one after another and that the accused petitioner himself made prayer to transfer the case from the court of Druto Bichar Tribunal, Court No.1 alleging bias of the learned Judge and accordingly the High Court Division passed an order. 

 "Wherefore, it is humbly prayed that, your Lordship would graciously be pleased to call for records issue a rule calling upon the opposite party to show cause as to why the proceeding in Druto Bichar Tribunal Case No. 12 of 2005 (arising out Dhanmondi) P.S. case No. 01 dated 01.03.2004) alleging an offence under section 333/326/109/34 of the Penal Code now pending in the Court of the Druto Bichar Tribunal No.1, Dhaka should not be transferred to and other competent court at Dhaka and after hearing the parties and cause shown may be pleased to make the rule absolute or be please to pass such other order/orders as to may seem fit and proper. 

 "Since learned Advocate for the petitioner and learned Deputy Attorney General are agreeable for transferring the case from the court of Druto Bichar Tribunal No.1 at Dhaka, we felt that it will be unnecessary to go deep into fact and other materials placed before this court through rule petition as well as supplementary affidavit counter affidavit and other applications in that view of the matter we are making the rule absolute." 

 11. It thus appears that according to the prayer of the petitioner himself pursuant to the submissions made by learned lawyers of both the parties the High Court Division made the rule absolute in favour of the petitioner allowing his prayer to transfer the case. 

 16. We have given consideration to the submissions made on behalf of the parties. From the conduct of the petitioner it appears that the submissions of the learned Attorney General that this application is ill designed tactics to delay the disposal of the case is not bereft of substance.
